question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -4 & 4\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ above. If the normal equation corresponding to the system $Ax=b$ is given below, what is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ -17 & 17\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-15 \\ c\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the system of linear equations and its corresponding normal equation shown above. What is the value of $a-b+c?$
current_example.worked_solution:
First, we write our system in matrix form as 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14159227/assets/3072a2a2d3f768327ac2a0aa806d468f9fc55c30133d5896a50817e8c2253d48.svg)

The normal equation corresponding to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,Ax & ={A}^{T}b \\ [\begin{aligned}4 & 8 \\ -3 & -6 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & -3 & -1 \\ 8 & -6 & -2\end{aligned}]x & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 8 \\ -3 & -6 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}80 & -60 & -20 \\ -60 & 45 & 15 \\ -20 & 15 & 5\end{aligned}]x & =[\begin{aligned}32 \\ -24 \\ -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a-b+c=(-20)-(-24)+(-20) = -16.
$$
